label: TMUA 2018 · Paper 2 · Question 14

hints.title: Draw the possible positions of Q
hints.body: Draw PR=2 and a ray from P at 30 degrees to PR. Since RQ=p, the point Q must also lie on the circle with centre R and radius p.
hints.recap: The required triangle exists where the ray meets the circle.
hints.pitfall: The ray goes in one direction from P; its backward extension is different.
hints.pause: Sketch the circle for a few different radii.

recall.reminder: The required triangle exists where the ray meets the circle.

hints.title: Find where the number of intersections changes
hints.body: Find the perpendicular distance from R to the ray. Also check the radius at which the circle passes through P.
hints.recap: A tangent has one contact point; a circle through P needs a separate check.
hints.pitfall: Q=P would give a side of length zero.
hints.pause: Count valid Q positions below, at and above both boundary radii.

recall.reminder: Dropping a perpendicular makes a right triangle. Use sine to find the perpendicular height.

solution:
Q is an intersection of the 30∘ ray from P with the circle centred at R of radius p. The perpendicular distance from R to the ray is 2sin30∘=1.

For p<1 there is no triangle; for p=1 the circle is tangent to the ray and there is one. For 1<p<2 there are two ray intersections. At p=2, one intersection coincides with P and is degenerate, leaving one valid triangle. For p>2, one line intersection moves behind P, leaving one on the required ray.

Therefore uniqueness holds for p=1 or p≥2. Answer E.
knowledgePattern: Count ray-circle intersections including tangent and degenerate boundaries
